estate_agency.law: Loi modifiée du 2 septembre 2011 réglementant l'accès aux professions d'artisan, de commerçant, d'industriel ainsi qu'à certaines professions libérales: art. 1 (business permit), art. 2 point 2° (definition), art. 10 (qualification, insurance). Loi modifiée du 21 septembre 2006 sur le bail à usage d'habitation, art. 5(1) (letting fees). Code civil (mandat, arts. 1984 ff.) for the mandate itself.
estate_agency.regulated: Yes. Art. 1: no one may habitually carry on a commercial activity for profit 'sans être titulaire d'une autorisation d'établissement' (business permit). Art. 10(1) requires a professional qualification or a specific accelerated training covering deontology, mandate law, sale, leases, 'la rémunération des agents immobiliers' and AML. Art. 10(2) requires professional liability insurance 'à tout moment' (at all times).
estate_agency.rule: No statute or regulation on dual mandates was found. The 2011 law defines the agent as an intermediary in real estate operations, 'généralement effectuée à titre de courtier dans le sens où l'agent immobilier met en relation deux personnes' (generally as a broker that brings two persons together), which fits a two-sided role. No disclosure or consent rule was located. Residential lettings are the exception: art. 5(1) of the 2006 law imposes a mandatory 50/50 split of agent fees between landlord and tenant.
estate_agency.quote: Loi 2011 art. 2 2°: '«agent immobilier»: the commercial activity of acting as intermediary in operations concerning real property. This intermediation is generally carried out as a broker, in the sense that the estate agent brings two persons together with a view to concluding a contract concerning real property.' Loi 2006 art. 5(1): 'Where an estate agent or other third party intervenes in the letting of a dwelling, the fees and charges of these persons are shared equally between the landlord and the tenant.' [... sont partagés par moitié entre le bailleur et le locataire.]
estate_agency.commission_both_sides: Residential lettings: yes, by law, split equally between landlord and tenant (2006 law art. 5(1), consolidated version applicable 02/10/2026). Sales: no statutory rule found, so it is contractual. Bill 7951 (proposition de loi, 2022) would cap sale commissions and make them payable only by the mandating party; its adoption is not confirmed.

aml.law: Loi modifiée du 12 novembre 2004 relative à la lutte contre le blanchiment et contre le financement du terrorisme: art. 2(1) point 10; art. 3(2) final subparagraph (added by Loi du 25 février 2021); art. 3(6). Supervisor: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AED).
aml.sale_scope: All real estate agency activity in sales, with no value threshold. Art. 2(1) point 10: 'les agents immobiliers, au sens de la loi modifiée du 2 septembre 2011 ..., établis ou agissant au Luxembourg, y compris lorsqu'ils agissent en qualité d'intermédiaires pour la location de biens immeubles, mais uniquement en ce qui concerne les transactions pour lesquelles le loyer mensuel est d'un montant égal ou supérieur à 10.000 euros'.
aml.letting_threshold: Lettings are covered only for transactions with monthly rent of EUR 10,000 or more (art. 2(1) point 10).
aml.both_parties: yes: art. 3(2) final subparagraph: 'In the case of a real estate transaction, the professionals referred to in Article 2(1), points 10 and 10bis, are obliged to apply due diligence measures to their clientele both towards the buyers and the sellers of the property.' [... aussi bien vis-à-vis des acquéreurs que des vendeurs du bien immobilier.]
aml.retention_trigger: Art. 3(6)(a)-(b): CDD copies and data, account books, business correspondence and analysis results, and transaction records are kept 'pendant cinq ans après la fin de la relation d'affaires avec le client ou après la date de la transaction conclue à titre occasionnel' (5 years after the end of the business relationship or after the date of the occasional transaction). Personal data must then be erased, without prejudice to longer periods under other laws.
aml.extension: Art. 3(6): supervisory authorities may require, in specific cases, retention 'pendant une période supplémentaire qui ne peut excéder cinq ans'. The professional also keeps personal data for a further 5 years where 'nécessaire pour la mise en œuvre efficace des mesures internes de prévention ou de détection' of ML/TF.
aml.id_copy: Required: art. 3(6)(a): professionals keep 'une copie ... des documents, des données et informations qui sont nécessaires pour se conformer aux obligations de vigilance' (a copy of the documents, data and information needed for CDD), including electronic-identification data.

accounting.trigger: Code de commerce art. 16 al. 2: documents under arts. 11 (books/journals), 12 (chart of accounts), 14 (supporting documents, letters received, copies of letters sent) and 15 (inventory and annual accounts) 'doivent être conservés pendant dix ans à partir de la clôture de l'exercice auquel ils se rapportent' (10 years from the close of the financial year to which they relate). Art. 16 al. 1: everything except the balance sheet and profit and loss account may be kept as a copy; the balance sheet and P&L must be kept in original.

limitation.trigger: Code civil art. 2257: prescription does not run on a conditional claim until the condition occurs, nor on a claim with a fixed date until that date. Commission conditional on completion therefore runs from the completed sale or letting.
limitation.law: Code civil art. 2262: 'Toutes les actions, tant réelles que personnelles, sont prescrites par trente ans' (30 years, general civil). Code de commerce art. 189: 'Les obligations nées à l'occasion de leur commerce entre commerçants ou entre commerçants et non-commerçants se prescrivent par dix ans si elles ne sont pas soumises à des prescriptions spéciales plus courtes' (10 years for obligations arising from commerce, including between a merchant and a non-merchant). The agent's commission claim is commercial, so 10 years. Code civil art. 2272 (1 year) covers merchants' actions 'pour les marchandises' sold to non-merchants, i.e. goods, not brokerage services.

id_copies.rule: No Luxembourg rule restricting ID copies outside AML was identified (not researched to a primary source; CNPD guidance not checked). Inside AML a copy is required (art. 3(6)(a)), and personal data must be erased after the retention period.
id_copies.law: Loi 12.11.2004 art. 3(6), 3(6bis) (GDPR applies to AML processing); otherwise GDPR Art. 5(1)(c).

unconfirmed: Dual agency in sales: no statute, regulation or AED/Chambre Immobilière rule located; classification left 'unclear'.
Sale commissions: whether bill 7951 (cap, commission payable only by the mandating party) or any later law has been adopted; not checked.
The AML text was read from the CSSF coordinated version hosted by the AED (to 27.07.2026), which is informational; the Mémorial/Legilux text was not compared.
Commission limitation: 10 years under Code de commerce art. 189 rests on the agent being a commerçant; no case law checked on whether a shorter special period applies.
No national rule on ID copies outside AML was researched (CNPD guidance and the 2013 identification law not checked; web-search budget exhausted).
